steps.name: Tenant schema migration: composite tenant PKs and legacy backfill
criteria: tenants table stores tenant_id, name, credential_hash with both columns unique
accounts gains tenant_id (default tnt_legacy_seed) and composite (tenant_id, id) primary key
entries and transactions gain tenant_id; entries' account/counterparty FKs become composite tenant-scoped
Migration is single file, expand-only, no DELETE/DROP; pre-existing rows backfill to tnt_legacy_seed
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-013/DDD-24 shape. tenants: tenant_id PK, name UNIQUE NOT NULL, credential_hash UNIQUE NOT NULL, GRANT SELECT,INSERT only (no UPDATE/DELETE). accounts: tenant_id DEFAULT 'tnt_legacy_seed' REFERENCES tenants; PK -> (tenant_id, id). entries: tenant_id REFERENCES tenants; FK(tenant_id,account_id)/(tenant_id,counterparty_id) -> accounts(tenant_id,id). transactions: plain tenant_id column, no PK change (UUIDs stay unique). One transaction, backfill before composite PK applied. Enables the legacy-backfilled environment's migration-safety proof.

steps.name: Tenant domain aggregate and sealed refusal taxonomy extension
criteria: Tenant aggregate holds {tenant_id, name, credential}; root-only value-typed fields, no constructor omits tenant_id
I10: tenant-name uniqueness enforced at construction, mirrors I9's account-uniqueness precedent
New sealed ViolationKind members tenant_already_exists and tenant_not_found added to the exhaustive switch
Cross-tenant account access reuses existing account_not_found member; I8 gets no new taxonomy member
steps.implementation_notes: Pure domain layer, no I/O. Contract shape: bounded-change — ProvisionTenant's declared delta is exactly one new Tenant row, complement-equality against Tenant/Account/Transaction collections (brief.md § Multitenancy Contract-shape table). Unit tests: property-based via rapid (pgregory.net/rapid), paired with state-delta/complement-equality assertions per this contract shape. Table-driven single-example tests are fallback only. Acceptance scenarios (godog) are pre-authored by DISTILL — this step's job is GREEN, not authoring new ones.

steps.name: TenantRepository and ProvisionTenant use case
criteria: TenantRepository port: Create and lookup-by-name, driven from a UnitOfWork, mirrors AccountRepository's read-decide-write shape
ProvisionTenant mints tenant_id/tenant_key via existing IDGenerator (tnt_/tk_ prefixes), stores sha256(tenant_key) hash only
Duplicate tenant name refused via domain's tenant_already_exists before any row is written
TenantKeyResolver port declared: pure-function, single lookup method, no write/touch method ever added
steps.implementation_notes: Reuse IDGenerator + crypto/sha256 (zero new dependency, DDD-26). TenantRepository mixes read/write inside one UnitOfWork — same accepted pattern as AccountRepository (atomic check-then-create), not a driving-port read/write mix. TenantKeyResolver: pure-function contract shape, exactly one method returning (tenantID string, ok bool, err error) — reviewer checks no second method is added. PBT via rapid for ProvisionTenant's bounded-change contract; Testcontainers-backed single-example test verifies TenantRepository wiring only.

steps.name: POST /tenants route: real provisioning, admin-gated
criteria: POST /tenants (requireOperatorKey, unmodified) replaces the scaffold with a real ProvisionTenant call
Response names tenant_id, name, tenant_key; tenant_key distinct from the platform-admin credential
Duplicate name refused 409 tenant_already_exists; wrong/missing/tenant-scoped credential refused 401 unidentified_caller
tenant_already_exists/tenant_not_found wired on both exhaustive-linted switch surfaces (domain and HTTP wire mapping)
steps.scenario_name: Provisioning a tenant issues a scoped credential
steps.implementation_notes: Un-skips (remove @pending) all 5 milestone-01 scenarios: Provisioning issues a scoped credential; Two tenants provisioned independently; Duplicate name refused; Tenant's own credential cannot provision; Unissued credential cannot provision. requireOperatorKey unchanged (DDD-22 EXTEND) — wrong/tenant credentials already refused by its existing string-compare, no new logic needed there. Adapter/integration test against real PostgreSQL (Testcontainers) stays single-example. demo-01..05 regression guard: this step touches no Makefile/AUTH surface, so unaffected.

phases.name: Slice 02 — Operate within a tenant, invisible to every other tenant

steps.name: I8 construction-time cross-tenant check in Post
criteria: Post gains a pre-construction cross-tenant check: from/to accounts naming different tenant_id refused before balance math runs
Cross-tenant refusal reuses the existing account_not_found member (I8 confirmed, no new taxonomy member)
Existing invariants I1, I4 unchanged in shape; one new refusal branch inside the same pure decision
steps.implementation_notes: Contract shape: pure-function (return-only), unchanged shape — the cross-check is a new refusal branch inside the same pure decision, not a new effect (brief.md § Multitenancy Contract-shape table). PBT via rapid, existing harness extended with a tenant-mismatch generator; do not rewrite Post's existing shape. End-to-end proof of this branch lands with step 02-04's route wiring, not here.

steps.name: Tenant-scoped AccountRepository and TransactionRepository
criteria: AccountRepository.{LockForUpdate,Create,ApplyDeltas,Get,All} take a required tenant_id string param, never TenantScope
Account-name uniqueness (I9/DDD-18) rescoped from global to (tenant_id, account_id)
TransactionRepository.Append/.Get gain required tenant_id; queries scoped by tenant_id at the WHERE clause
EntriesFor/TrialBalance/ComputedBalances gain TenantScope (closed ScopedToTenant/Unscoped constructors), never a nullable string
steps.implementation_notes: TenantScope lives in internal/app/ports: type TenantScope struct{unexported}; ScopedToTenant(tenantID)/Unscoped() constructors; Resolve() (tenantID string, scoped bool). Only read ports with a legitimate unscoped state get TenantScope — write paths and single-tenant reads keep plain required tenant_id (construction-time enforcement, I8). Contract shape: bounded-change (existing pattern, extended) — complement-equality universe narrowed to one tenant's rows. PBT via rapid + single-example Testcontainers adapter tests.

steps.name: requireTenantKey and requireTenantKeyOrOperatorKey middlewares
criteria: bearerToken/isOperatorKey primitive extracted from requireOperatorKey, shared by all three middlewares
requireTenantKey resolves the bearer token via TenantKeyResolver; injects a typed tenant_id context key or refuses 401
requireTenantKeyOrOperatorKey tries the OperatorKey compare first (byte-identical to today), falls back to tenant lookup
POST /accounts, POST /transfers, GET /accounts/{id} mounted under a requireTenantKey-only chi group (DDD-23 Option C)
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-22: EXTEND requireOperatorKey (factor out the shared header primitive), CREATE NEW the two tenant middlewares (keyed DB lookup differs in mechanism from static-secret compare). Contract shape: bounded-change — context annotation only; assert the middleware calls no driven port with a Create/Apply/Append verb, only TenantKeyResolver (a read). Typed context key, not a bare string, so a handler cannot read the wrong context value.

steps.name: Wire tenant-scoped routes and dual-mode entries
criteria: POST /accounts, POST /transfers, GET /accounts/{id} pass the caller's tenant_id from context into Ledger calls
GET /accounts/{id}/entries dual-mode: tenant_key sees own entries; unscoped OperatorKey call byte-identical to today
Cross-tenant read/write refused as account_not_found (404); malformed/missing credential refused 401 before tenant logic runs
Existing single-tenant invariants I1, I3, I4, I7 hold unchanged from the caller's point of view
steps.scenario_name: A newly onboarded tenant operates invisibly to an existing tenant
steps.implementation_notes: Un-skips the walking skeleton plus all 7 milestone-02 scenarios (tests/acceptance/multitenancy/milestone-02-operate-within-a-tenant.feature): same-name reuse across tenants, account invisible to another tenant, cross-tenant transfer refused, single-tenant invariants unchanged, malformed credential refused, entries scoped, unscoped entries byte-identical. requireTenantKeyOrOperatorKey (02-03) gates entries; requireTenantKey gates accounts/transfers. Acceptance scenarios pre-authored by DISTILL — GREEN only, no new authoring. Adapter tests against real PostgreSQL stay single-example.

steps.name: Demo tenant credential, Makefile AUTH split, and ledgercore suite fix (OPS-13, scope expanded 2026-09-04)
criteria: LEDGEROPS_DEMO_TENANT_KEY env var seeded to tnt_legacy_seed's credential (mirrors LEDGEROPS_OPERATOR_KEY pattern)
Makefile AUTH repointed to the seeded tenant key; new OPERATOR_AUTH variable added for admin-only calls
demo-01..03 and chaos-01 recipe bodies stay byte-for-byte unchanged; only AUTH's value changes
scripts/race/main.go gains RACE_TENANT_KEY (defaults to LEDGEROPS_DEMO_TENANT_KEY's value) for account/transfer calls

tests/acceptance/ledgercore's own test world (ledger_world.go) seeds/uses a tenant credential bound to tnt_legacy_seed for POST /accounts, POST /transfers, GET /accounts/{id} step definitions, replacing the hardcoded OperatorKey use on those three routes only — OperatorKey stays correct for every other ledgercore step (unscoped reads, provisioning-adjacent admin calls)
go test ./tests/acceptance/ledgercore/... returns to its pre-multitenancy pass rate (93/93, or the project's existing baseline) — CI's blocking integration job is restored
steps.implementation_notes: OPS-10/OPS-11/OPS-13 DEVOPS-inherited (DESIGN recorded OPS-10; DELIVER discovered and self-recorded OPS-11 and OPS-13; DELIVER implements all three). tnt_legacy_seed's credential_hash must correspond to a known plaintext seeded at migration/startup — composition root wire-then-probe (Earned Trust, Core Principle 13) should refuse startup with health.startup.refused if the seed lookup fails. race-02/race-03 currently call now-tenant_key-only routes via RACE_OPERATOR_KEY — this fixes them before slice-02 lands (review-gate action item 1). OPS-13 (added 2026-09-04, feature-delta.md § Wave: DELIVER / Upstream Issues): tests/acceptance/ledgercore/ledger_world.go hardcodes OperatorKey for every request (ledger_world.go:144,480), which now fails 80/93 scenarios in CI's blocking integration job since DDD-23 made POST /accounts/POST /transfers/GET /accounts/{id} tenant-key-only. Fix mirrors OPS-11 exactly: seed a tenant credential for this suite's own world, repoint only the three affected step definitions' Authorization header, leave every other step's OperatorKey usage untouched. Single-example integration verification (Makefile/script/world.go wiring, not an invariant).

phases.name: Slice 03 — Verify one tenant's books without seeing another's

steps.name: Tenant-scoped GET /health/trial-balance
criteria: VerifyBooks accepts TenantScope; tenant-scoped call filters entries/accounts to that tenant, unscoped aggregates platform-wide
GET /health/trial-balance?tenant_id= scopes the query using OperatorKey (existing DDD-22 mapping); unscoped call keeps succeeding
Unprovisioned tenant_id refused 404 tenant_not_found before any scan runs
Tenant-scoped verdict names only that tenant's drift (account, delta); never mentions another tenant
steps.implementation_notes: TransactionRepository.TrialBalance/ComputedBalances already gained TenantScope in step 02-02; this step wires the ?tenant_id= query param through VerifyBooks. Contract shape: pure-function (return-only) — read-only, universe = scope's declared entry set (brief.md § Multitenancy Contract-shape table). Regression assertion: unscoped call's result byte-identical to the pre-feature contract (DoD item 3a). PBT via rapid for the scoped-filter logic; single-example adapter test for the query wiring.

steps.name: Console verdict dual-mode compat
criteria: GET /console/verdict (shared verdictHandler) keeps answering unscoped OperatorKey calls byte-identical to today's shape/status
Tenant's clean books report YES independent of another tenant's drift; drift named without exposing other tenants
Checking an unprovisioned tenant is refused, not silently answered YES
No account belonging to another tenant appears in any tenant-scoped or unscoped response
steps.scenario_name: A tenant's clean books report YES independent of another tenant's state
steps.implementation_notes: Un-skips milestone-03's 5 scenarios: clean books YES, drift named without leaking, unprovisioned tenant refused, unscoped trial-balance byte-identical, unscoped console verdict byte-identical. verdictHandler is shared between both routes by construction (cannot disagree) — this step's dual-mode fix on one fixes both, per the console-compatibility hard constraint. @console-compat scenarios assert shape/status match; byte-for-byte golden-diff tightening is a DELIVER action item (review-gate finding 2), not required here.

steps.name: demo-04 target and new CI gate jobs
criteria: demo-04 provisions a tenant and posts its first transfer on a clean clone, emits tenant_onboard_transfer_seconds
tenant-isolation-gates CI job asserts 100% cross-tenant refusal and per-tenant trial-balance leak-free across the suite

Ten required jobs gate main; existing eight unchanged, two new (tenant-isolation-gates, console-compat) blocking

Both gate branch protection alongside existing invariant-gates.
